proposals.rationale: Inverse directional object properties in the same namespace — antonyms expressing opposite directions of the same transfer relationship, not the same concept.
Sibling enumeration individuals in the same audit-type classification: 1st-party vs 2nd-party PCF verification — same classification axis, distinct values.
Sibling enumeration individuals: 1st-party vs 3rd-party PCF verification — same classification axis, distinct values.
Sibling enumeration individuals: 2nd-party vs 3rd-party PCF verification — same classification axis, distinct values.
Parallel datatype properties measuring product verification share for different parties (1PVS vs 2PVS); same structural role, distinct party-scope — not interchangeable.
Parallel datatype properties for 1PVS vs 3PVS; same structural role across different party scopes.
Parallel datatype properties for 2PVS vs 3PVS; same structural role across different party scopes.

Both are the CAD Trust project GUID — identical label, identical definition, both are identifiers for the same CAD Trust project entity; comet-ver is a more published layer so it is preferred as canonical.
Both are the CAD Trust project GUID with identical label and definition; the comet-ver instance is the more foundational published-layer definition.
RSInputMaterial is a domain-constrained subtype of Material scoped to ResponsibleSteel Annex 1 ferrous inputs; comet:Material is the general input/output substance concept that encompasses it.

comet-cn:Baseline is the ISO 14068-1 general concept of quantified GHG emissions for a base period; ProcessGasBaseline is a highly specific counterfactual baseline restricted to captured process gases in steelmaking CCUS credits.
GWP100Value is the class representing a GWP100 measurement object; gwpValue is the datatype property slot carrying the numeric factor on that class — a is broader than b.
a is a specific SDG 1 (No Poverty) co-benefit picklist instance; b is the general CoBenefit class — a is a named individual falling under the class, making a narrower.
a is a specific SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) co-benefit picklist instance; b is the general CoBenefit class — a is a named individual falling under the class, making a narrower.
a is a specific SDG 4 (Quality Education) co-benefit picklist instance; b is the general CoBenefit class — a is a named individual falling under the class, making a narrower.
a is a specific SDG 5 (Gender Equality) co-benefit picklist instance; b is the general CoBenefit class — a is a named individual falling under the class, making a narrower.

comet:Site is the concept of a physical facility, while siteAuditBoundary is a descriptive property of the boundary defined at certification time — the class is broader than the attribute it subsumes.
a is the general biogenic carbon content property; b is scoped specifically to packaging per declared unit (TfS field), making a broader and b narrower.
Identical labels and identical definition (manufacturing route, BOF/EAF/etc.) in two namespaces; comet-pcf is a published layer while comet-rs is an extension, making comet-pcf the canonical term.

Both record the calendar date of a retirement event; they differ in domain context (carbon neutrality claim vs. EAC retirement) but represent the same temporal data point, with the EAC term residing in the more foundational published layer.

Both capture the end date of a period; comet-cn scopes it to reporting period in a carbon-neutrality context, but the underlying temporal concept is the same; comet is the more foundational namespace.
Both capture the start date of a period; comet-cn restricts scope to reporting period, but the underlying temporal property is the same; comet is more foundational.
Both hold the awarded rating score or grade; comet-ver is the published ontology layer preferred over the cadtrust source schema.
EAC is the certificate instrument itself; EACSpotPrice is a market price observation for that instrument — related as instrument-to-price but not the same concept.
hasSPL is an object property linking an entity to its Sourcing Progress Level; splLevel is the datatype property carrying the integer 1–4 level value — structurally related but not the same concept.
Both are properties describing the type/provider of a rating; comet-ver is the published ontology layer preferred over the cadtrust source schema.

Both measure biogenic carbon content; comet-tfs scopes to per-declared-unit (TfS field 128), while comet-pcf is the general property — semantically the same measurement; comet-pcf is the published layer and preferred canonical.

Both are severity properties on non-conformity findings in audit/verification contexts; comet-rs:nonConformitySeverity is RS-scoped with enumerated values (major/minor), while comet-ver:severity is the more general published-layer property that should be canonical.

Both are identifier fields for a CAD Trust project — one on the source cadtrust schema, one on the COMET attestation object; comet-ver is the published ontology layer preferred over the cadtrust extension.

cadtrust:cobenefit is a field capturing which co-benefit a project achieves; comet-eac:CoBenefit is the class defining SDG co-benefits — same concept, different representation layer; comet-eac is the published ontology layer.

Both represent the share of primary vs secondary data (0–100); comet-sc models it as a Class while comet-tfs is a DatatypeProperty carrying the value, but they encode the same measurement concept; comet-sc (published layer) is preferred over the TfS extension.
Both mark the end date of a defined period; cadtrust scopes to estimation period, comet is a general period end property; comet is the foundational canonical term.

Both represent total GWP including biogenic for a product carbon footprint; comet-tfs adds TfS-specific position accounting (T1 = A+B+C+D+E+F+G+H) but covers the same measurement; comet-pcf is the published layer preferred over the TfS extension.

Both are 'not-applicable' sentinel individuals sharing the same semantic intent (field does not apply), but scoped to different TfS position slots (CCU vs WI), so they cannot be merged without losing positional context.
hasDataQualityRating is an object property linking to a rating; comet-ver:Rating is the class being linked to — a property and its range class are semantically related but not the same concept.

GWP100Value is a reusable value object class for any GWP100 factor; totalGWP is a specific property slot on a PCF record holding the total GWP — related (totalGWP likely uses GWP100Value instances) but not the same concept.

Both model 'principle' within their respective standards (ISO 14068-1 carbon neutrality vs. ResponsibleSteel production) — structurally analogous but semantically governed by entirely different frameworks and not interchangeable.
Both encode the 'cut-off' approach individual but are typed to different TfS position slots (RC = recycled content, WI = waste incineration); same concept, incompatible positional scope.

Shared label masks a conceptual divergence: comet-cn:VerificationOpinion is the whole ISO 14068-1 §12 independent verification statement/process, while comet-ver:VerificationOpinion is the formal opinion type enumeration (unqualified/qualified/adverse/disclaimer) — related but not the same concept.

comet-cn:Principle is a class for ISO 14068-1 carbon-neutrality principles; comet-rs:principleAssessed is an object property pointing to a principle in a responsible-sourcing audit context — different domains and OWL roles, though the 'principle' concept overlaps.
b is specifically the biogenic carbon content of packaging per declared unit (a narrow datatype property), whereas a is the general Class for biogenic carbon per ISO 14067; a is broader.

Both are object properties linking an entity to its scope/boundary definition; comet-cn operates in a carbon-neutrality context, comet-tfs in a PCF boundary-declaration context — same structural intent with minor scope difference; neither namespace is clearly more foundational for this concept.
GWP100Value is a class for a single GWP factor value; hasGWPBreakdown is an object property linking to a structured breakdown of GWP positions — related in the GWP domain but different concepts.

Both denote material recovered after consumer use (post-consumer / end-of-life scrap); the label of a explicitly includes 'Post-consumer' as a synonym, making these near-identical concepts with minor framing differences.

a is a picklist enumeration value labeling a type of validation activity; b is a class representing the validation record artifact — related in domain (project design validation) but different ontological roles.
a is an identifier field pointing to a specific co-benefit instance within CAD Trust, while b is the general SDG co-benefit Class; a is narrower (an identifier for an instance of b's concept).
Both represent the start date of a bounded time period; comet:TimePeriod.startDate is the more foundational definition and a is a domain-specific usage of that concept.

Both represent an applicable Global Warming Potential value; a is a data field in the CAD Trust AEF authorization table, b is the formal GWP100Value class — same concept, with b being the more foundational definition.
Same reasoning as T2 pair above: a is the GWP field in the AEF actions table, b is the canonical GWP100Value class; closeMatch with b as canonical.
Same reasoning: a is the GWP field in the AEF holdings table, b is the canonical GWP100Value class; same concept expressed in a domain-specific field vs ontology class.

ISO21930PCR is defined as a SuMPO PCR formally based on ISO 21930, while SuMPOPCRDocument is the broader SuMPO-issued PCR (ISO 21930 or EN 15804); they overlap heavily but ISO21930PCR is a specific subtype of SuMPOPCRDocument.

Both denote a 'certified' status in the carbon-project lifecycle, but a is a picklist enumeration value while b is an Individual in the crediting-notes layer; same concept, different modeling level, so closeMatch rather than exactMatch.

Both capture the end date of an accounting/reporting period; estimation period end and reporting period end are near-synonymous in carbon-project context, though 'estimation' vs 'reporting' introduces a slight scope difference.
a is an identifier field for a validation event, while b is the class representing the full project-design ValidationRecord; a references an instance of b's concept but is not the same concept.
a is the general Site class (physical facility), while b is an object property pointing to an audited site; b references instances of a's class but is a property, not the class itself.

a is the Class representing biogenic carbon per ISO 14067, while b is a DatatypeProperty for the numeric biogenic carbon content value per declared unit in TfS; different modeling levels (class vs datatype property) but closely related in domain.

CCQI (Carbon Credit Quality Initiative) is a specific rating scheme instance — a particular value of rating_type — while comet-ver:Rating is the general class for any independent quality rating; a is narrower.

a is a field holding the specific value awarded in a rating, which is an attribute of b (the Rating class for independent quality assessment); a is a property-level concept that is narrower than the class b.
a is a data-field holding the name of a rating, which is an attribute of b (the Rating class representing an independent quality assessment); a is narrower and property-level, b is a class.

a is the general class for a physical facility or production location, while b is documentation of a visit to such a site during verification; related but distinct — one is the entity, the other is an activity record.
CDP is a specific rating-scheme picklist value, while comet-ver:Rating is the general Rating class; a names a particular rating provider, b is the broader concept.

a is the general Class for an input/output substance, while b is a datatype property recording the geographic origin region of a material supplier; b is an attribute of instances of a, not the same concept.

a is the GWP100 factor for a specific gas species, while b is the total GWP of an entire product carbon footprint including biogenic; they are related numeric GWP quantities but at different levels of aggregation.

Both use the term 'standardRef' but a is the PCF cross-sectoral standard class while b is a property on a VerificationClaim pointing to the verification standard; same naming pattern, different domains and modeling levels.

a is a property for biogenic carbon content specifically (per ISO 14067), while b is an object property linking to a carbon content breakdown structure; related in domain but not interchangeable — b is a structural link, a is a specific biogenic value.
Both are carbon-content properties per declared unit but cover distinct carbon pools (biogenic vs recycled); they are siblings in the carbon-content domain, not the same concept.

a is an identifier for a specific estimation record, while b is the project-level GUID; both are CAD Trust identifiers but at different entity levels (estimation vs project), so related but not the same concept.

a is the general Class for a manufacturing or transformation step, while b is a specific datatype property for power generated from process gases in MWh; b is an energy-quantity property associated with a process, not a synonym for the Process class itself.

a is an attribute describing the type of validation performed, while b is the ValidationRecord class itself; they are related within the validation domain but at different levels and different semantic roles.
a is a scalar GWP100 factor value, while b is an object property linking to a GWP position breakdown structure; related in domain but a is a scalar and b is a structural link to a complex breakdown.
a is an identifier for a specific project location within CAD Trust, while b is the project-level GUID; they are related CAD Trust identifiers but at different entity levels (location vs project).

a is a stakeholder identifier field within the CAD Trust data model, while b is the class for a CAD Trust project attestation record; they share the CAD Trust namespace but are at different levels (entity identifier vs attestation class).
